GROOVE STATION

Seven styles of house, start to finish in your browser. Every sound is generated live — there are no audio files to load. Tap a pad, get a loop; tap four, get a groove.

SOUND

How it works

Pads A B C D
Each row is an instrument, each pad is a one-bar loop. Tap to bring it in, tap the lit pad to drop it out.
Instant / Bar sync
Instant is the default: a pad takes effect the moment you press it, and anything already playing on that row is cut dead. Switch to Bar sync if you'd rather changes wait for the next barline so nothing can land off-grid.
Performance FX
One row, all hold-to-use, all instant — nothing waits for a beat or a bar. Hold for as long as you want the effect, let go and you're straight back.
Echo H — a tight dotted-sixteenth repeat of the sound you're pressing on. The delay line is fed constantly, so the echo is of what just played, not of what happens next.
Flanger U and Phaser I — sweeping movement, flanger the jet whoosh, phaser the rotating speaker. Both sweep in time: one pass every two bars, and every bar.
Gate J — chops the whole mix into sixteenths. Hold it under a chord for a trance gate, or stab it for a bar to break up a loop.
Tape stop O — the brake. Pitch and speed fall together over about half a second, like a deck losing power, and it spins back up when you let go.
Bass cut L — ducks the kick and bass about 24 dB rather than muting them.
Lock deck
The second deck. When you land on something you like, hit LOCK (Shift+L) and that loop is frozen — kit, pads, patterns, chance, everything — and keeps playing on its own. You're then free to tear the live layer apart and build the next thing underneath it, and the A/B BLEND knob crossfades between them. That's a DJ transition, and it's the one move a single-deck groove box can't make. Hit LOCK again to clear it. The locked deck ignores your live mutes on purpose, and follows the tempo if you push it, because it's a frozen copy of the pattern rather than a recording of the audio.
Mangle
G, hold. The selected track re-rolls its pattern every bar while you hold it, then snaps back to exactly what it was. Nothing is overwritten, so you can lean on it for eight bars and lose nothing. The dice and the chance rows were always the most interesting thing in here and they were buried in the editor — this puts them under your finger.
Half time
P, hold. The groove drops to half speed while the transport keeps running at the same tempo, so it stays in sync and rejoins cleanly. The locked deck keeps its own time, so you can half-time the live layer against a steady loop.
DJ filter
The knob beside the FX row, and the one control worth playing with. Centre is off; turn left to sweep the low-pass down, right to sweep the high-pass up. Resonance comes in on its own as you leave centre.
Why there are only two knobs
There used to be six. DELAY, SPACE, CRUSH and DRIVE are gone, and their jobs are now fixed at the right values. SPACE in particular was sitting at 43% from power-on, feeding every track into a two-and-a-half second hall — which is why things sounded washed before you touched anything. The machine now powers on sounding finished. Reverb and delay are still there, set per kit where they belong: a touch of room on the clap and percussion, more on the keys, most on the vocal, and none at all on the kick or bass.
The sounds each kit uses
Press and hold an instrument name (or right-click it) to swap its engine. Worth knowing what's in there: M1 organ bass is the Show Me Love / New York garage bass — a triangle at the root with a square an octave and a fifth above, no third anywhere, which is why it sits under any chord. Piano 16 is the bright, hard, slightly tacky stab that cuts through a busy mix where a real piano would vanish. Filtered strings is the big rising swell — a wide ensemble behind a resonant filter that opens as the phrase lands. S-MAN GARAGE is the kit built around all three.
Perc row characters
r rim   s shaker   c conga   d ride   t tom   b bell   n finger snap. Click a step repeatedly to cycle through them.
Remix
Swaps the keys or the bass for another style's engine — soulful piano over a dub tech groove, organ bass under deep house. Press it until something surprises you. X remixes, C puts the stock sounds back.
Fill
Drops a one-bar snare and tom roll, then returns to the pattern.
Rec
Captures live audio to a .webm file you can drop straight into a DAW.
Audio: smooth or tight
Smooth is the default and uses a larger output buffer, which is what stops crackling — especially on Windows and on Bluetooth earbuds. Tight uses the smallest buffer the browser allows for the fastest possible response, at the risk of crackle. Reload the page after changing it.
Your work is kept
Every pattern, chance value, step count, level and mute is saved as you go, per kit, and comes back when you reopen the page. Switching kits and back keeps your edits too. The button at the bottom restores the factory patterns for the kit you're on — it asks once before it does.
Keys
Space play/stop   1–7 select instrument   Q W E R launch pad for it   A S D F launch scene   G roll the dice   Z undo   Y redo   K keep   , . step count   [ ] tempo
FX keys
H echo   U flanger   I phaser   J gate   O tape stop   P half time   G mangle   L bass cut. Hold them; they release when you do. Shift+L locks the deck.
